Local Design Lab · final specification pass

One card, three densities, two grains

Financials is one card at three densities, not three products. Subject and payer are separate dimensions and the ledger now proves it. And the Process card stopped treating a waitlisted child as a chip.

Compact 221 · Summary 450 · Detail 653 Process 297 · aligned 228typecheck rc=0

Financials densities one card no new primitives

PlacementdensityspanRendersHeight
Compactcompact1due line · 2–4 charge lines · payment health · three actions221
Summarycompact"row"full Current Period / Past Due / Payment450
Detailexpanded"row"ledger-first, filters, periods653

No new density system — FocusPanelCardDensity and FocusPanelCardSpan already express all three. All three read the same evidence, compute nothing, and expose the same canonical actions: density selects how many of the card's questions a placement answers, never ownership, the arithmetic, or which actions exist.

The compact card deliberately does not reconcile. A card that half-reconciles is the worst of both.

Recommendation

Compact (span 1) is the default placement. At 221px it sits beside Household (216) and Readiness (188) and answers what most processes actually ask — is money owed, can I act. Full-row summary is for billing-heavy contexts only: at 1023×450 its left column runs to dead space unless the operator is genuinely working the money.

Subject and payer two dimensions

DimensionQuestionValues
Charge subjectwho or what is this forHousehold · Avery · Riley
Payerwho is responsible for payingJordan · Taylor · Funding

Never collapsed. A charge for Avery may be paid by Jordan; a household charge has no child subject at all. The two filters compose — all activity for Avery, Jordan's payments, Avery's charges allocated to Jordan, household-only charges. Both are projections over canonical truth, never separate ledgers.

New gap F7 — and it is the one that blocks this

charges has job_id, schedule_id, subscription_id and no subject column. A child-specific charge cannot be attributed today, so “all activity for Avery” is unanswerable from canonical truth. Smallest fix: a nullable subject_entity_type / subject_entity_id on charges, polymorphic exactly as documents already is, with null meaning household-level.

Add charge both dimensions stated

Applies to = financial subject. Charge to = financial responsibility. Two inputs, each governed by the template — required, inherited, fixed, selectable or overridable. No childcare semantics in shared action code.

Process card — four layers, six scenarios, one implementation

The previous version reduced Avery's Waitlist to a chip. It is now a row — her avatar, her stage, since-when, and her own action. Case truth and participant truth are separate first-class layers:

  1. 1Case journey — the configured stage spine
  2. 2Case work + actions whose SUBJECT is the case
  3. 3Participant state — first-class, at its own grain
  4. 4Child-scoped actions, sitting ON the child's row so the operator can never mistake which entity an action affects
ScenarioCaseChildrenHeight
A · from TourTourAvery Waitlisted · Riley Tour297

D · scoped to RileyTourRiley ordered first, emphasised297
E · divergentEnrollingAvery Waitlisted · Riley Enrolling297
F · alignedTourcollapsed to one line228

Lens chip: removed. The workspace already says which Work View the operator is in, and a lens cannot change stage or work — so the chip restated navigation context at the cost of card space.

The card grew, 221 → 297, and that is the point. The old Journey + What's Next pair could not express child divergence at all, and the chip version understated it. Still −36% against 467px across two cards, and −51% when children are aligned. Subject ambiguity: eliminated.

Order: F0 → F7 → F5 → M1 → P1 → G1 → F3/F6, with card registration happening per card as its read model lands — never as a batch, never ahead of the truth it projects.
